g.text: next dashboard: step.sh records this run + invalidates for the next one (round-robin, 11 × 10)
1 · Invalidate the caches (before every single measurement)
step.sh → invalidate.sh → run_sql.py runs sql/90_invalidate_caches.sql on the setup warehouse: SET TBLPROPERTIES on all 8 tables (new Delta versions, same data)
+ REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW … FULL, so neither the SQL result cache nor the dashboard cache can serve the next Refresh. Done before every single measurement (step.sh:5-7).
2 · Open the published dashboard with a bigger timing buffer
navigate_page with initScript performance.setResourceTimingBufferSize(10000): runs before any page script, so no request timing is dropped (default buffer: 250 entries).
Then evaluate_script runs measure.js in the page. It first waits until this page load has settled; the load is reported as the subsequent load (step 4).
3 · First load (cold) = Refresh click → last dashboard-query response
Page settled → click Refresh, tClick = performance.now() (measure.js:21-24). settle(tClick) polls /lakeview-query/ entries started after the click until none is new for 10 s (8-19).
first_load_s = last responseEnd − tClick (measure.js:25, 28). Cold: the queries execute on the bench warehouse, 0 result-cache hits.
4 · Subsequent load (cached) = navigation start → last dashboard-query response
The page load from step 2: settle(0) with the same rule as step 3, counted from t = 0 = navigation start (measure.js:20). subsequent_load_s = latest responseEnd (measure.js:27).
Served by the dashboard cache. In the script this load is timed before the Refresh: publishing pre-warms the dashboard cache, so no page navigation is ever cold.
5 · Values come back as the evaluate_script tool result
The function returns {subsequent_load_s, first_load_s, n_requests_*}. The MCP hands it back to the agent as the tool result (measure.js:26-29).
The browser writes nothing to disk.
6 · Record the run (agent copies the numbers) and move to the next dashboard
The agent passes the two numbers as arguments to the next ./step.sh call → record.sh:4 appends one line to results/browser_runs.jsonl, then the caches are invalidated for the next dashboard.
11 dashboards round-robin × 10 rounds = 110 measurements. One unrecorded warm-up load per dashboard before round 1.
7 · Aggregate (mean ± sd, Welch t) and cross-check against the warehouse
report.py: mean ± sd per variant and deltas with Welch t (report.py:22-34) → results/browser_<variant>.json, summary.md.
server_side.py: per Refresh, first query start → last query end from system.query.history as an independent warehouse-side check (PRO only).
